paragraphs: Berakhot 15a (compare [Berakhot 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.15b.27)) has him reciting before Rava. [Niddah 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.20b.7) relates that Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur’s mother, sent blood to Rava. Rav Ovadiah was sitting before him; he smelled it and said, “This is blood of desire.” Hyman reads this as Rava smelling it, but Yuchasin takes the subject to be Rav Ovadiah. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2834&lang=en) says that Yuchasin erred; yet this is also the view of the [Rashba on Niddah 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashba_on_Niddah.20b.1): “It seems to me that Rav Ovadiah smelled it, for Rava was not expert in blood.” He develops the argument at length there.
And in Bava Batra 22b (compare [Bava Batra 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.22a.3)), Rava permitted Rav Yoshiyah and Rav Ovadiah the marketplace.[^3]

notes.text: The verb means “smelled it,” not “was on his way.” Whether Rava or Ovadiah smelled the blood is exactly the disagreement Hyman reports; the English keeps that disagreement visible.

The consulted Niddah 20b has Ovadiah seated before Rava in the Ifra Hormiz blood episode, distinct from the adjacent Rabbi Elazar/Ami episode. Rashba on Niddah 20b, Gerlitz edition published by Oraita, explicitly argues that Ovadiah smelled the blood and that Rava was not expert in blood. Hyman’s plain-sense Rava reading and reported disagreement remain visible; Yuchasin and Seder HaDorot exact editions were not inspected here.

Heilprin identifies Rava as the one who smelled the blood. The Rashba identifies Ovadiah and argues that the text’s express mention of Ovadiah sitting before Rava gives him a role in the episode. The linked Bava Batra gives Rabbi Yoshiyah and Rav Ovadiah permission to establish a regular place of sale.
